facts.text: Emmitsburg was founded in 1785 by William Emmit, a pioneer settler, and the town was originally called Silver Fancy before adopting its current name.
The town sits just 0.3 miles south of the Mason-Dixon line, placing it right on the historic border between Maryland and Pennsylvania.
Emmitsburg hosts Catholic pilgrimage sites: the National Shrine Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes on Mount St. Mary's campus and the Basilica and National Shrine of St. Mary's.
The National Shrine of St. Mary's was home to Elizabeth Ann Seton, the first native-born U.S. citizen to be canonized, whose convent, school, and hospital began there.
During the Civil War, Union forces fortified Emmitsburg to halt a Confederate invasion in June 1863, making the town a key defensive point.

The former Saint Joseph College campus now houses the National Emergency Training Center, including the Emergency Management Institute, National Fire Academy, and National Fallen Firefighters Memorial.
